corrections: Removed fixed 70/20/10 test ratios and clarified that test-layer allocation follows risk, feedback time and maintenance cost.
Clarified that unit tests need not mock every dependency and integration tests may cover varying component boundaries.
Reframed code coverage as execution evidence rather than a correctness target; removed near-100-percent prescriptions for core code.
Clarified that consumer-driven contracts complement rather than replace integration and end-to-end tests, and only detect incompatibility when relevant provider verification runs.
Corrected percentile wording and explained why service P99 values cannot be directly composed; the independence calculation is only an illustrative probability model.
Qualified rate-limiter latency claims because queuing, limiter overhead and shared-resource contention can still affect admitted requests.
Updated gomock ownership: github.com/golang/mock is archived and go.uber.org/mock is the maintained fork.
Clarified Go fuzzing capability boundaries: seeds are recommended but optional, properties must be asserted, and race discovery requires race instrumentation and a triggering schedule.
Reviewed TDD terminology as a development workflow rather than a coverage guarantee, and retained trade-offs as guidance rather than universal rules.

relationSuggestions.reason: Contract tests add fast service-boundary compatibility checks to a layered test strategy.
Test doubles are one isolation technique for selected lower-level tests, not a mandatory definition of unit testing.
TDD produces fast executable examples while the test pyramid governs the broader portfolio of test scopes.
Property-based fuzz targets complement example-based unit and component tests.
Load tests verify performance characteristics not established by functional test layers.
